subject: Re: Acme Health - streaming follow-up & test plan
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & streaming UX notes from today's demo

Thanks Marissa, very helpful recap.

We can prioritize triage and clinical-summary as the two flows to run first; triage+followup can be third. Priya will drop a redacted sample prompt set and traffic profile by EOD tomorrow.

Observations from our internal review of the demo:
- We saw 2/10 streaming cases where the stream stopped mid-sentence and on resume the model repeated the last 3 tokens.
- For compliance we require a machine-readable end marker (we suggested "assistant_stop") and that the marker is emitted >= 99% of the time.

Can you confirm whether Redwood enforces stop-sequence detection server-side for streaming responses, or if that is typically handled client-side? Would appreciate a short working session next week.

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-health.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme-health.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme - streaming follow-up & test plan

Looping in Dev and Neha to scope a streaming test per Acme's confirm. Short version: reproduce repeat-on-resume, enforce assistant_stop marker, and run across our two recommended models.

Dev: please prioritize a 90-minute slot on Dedicated for a reproducibility run. Useful axes: chunk size, server-side stop enforcement, and KV cache TTL.
Neha: can you draft success criteria (p50/p90/p99 latency, mid-sentence stop incidence, assistant_stop coverage)? Aim for a draft by 2026-03-02 EOD so we can share with Acme.

I will propose two times for a working session next week once we have the test plan.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-health.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - scheduling reproducibility run

I scheduled a 90-minute reproducibility window on Dedicated for 2026-03-04 10:00-11:30 PST. The test harness can toggle: small-centroid-3b vs med-opt-7b, streaming chunk sizes (64B/256B/1kB), and server-side stop enforcement on/off.

I'll instrument per-token timestamps, token-id hashes, and a stop-marker flag. If we see token repetition on resume we will capture a 20-token pre/post window for analysis.

Attaching brief harness notes: streaming_test_plan_v1.docx (see attachments).

- Dev

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-health.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T10:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - streaming test plan draft (summary)

Hi all

Inline summary of the test plan I've uploaded to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-Acme-evals

- Flows: triage, clinical-summary, triage+followup (synthetic + replayed sanitized traffic; ~10k tokens total)
- Models: small-centroid-3b, med-opt-7b
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 token latency, percent mid-sentence stops, percent responses with assistant_stop, token repetition rate
- Test controls: chunk size (64B/256B/1kB), server-side vs client-side stop enforcement, KV cache TTL (1s/10s/60s)
- Success criteria: p90 latency <= 350ms on 3b under target QPS, mid-sentence stops < 1%, assistant_stop present in >= 99% of responses

I'll publish the full doc and share a calendar invite for the working session after Dev's run.

Neha Kapoor
SRE / Product Reliability
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
